data.name: Awamir
data.long_meaning: Awamir is a name derived from the Arabic word ‘Awam’ meaning ‘gifted’ and ‘mir’ meaning ‘warrior’. The name signifies a gifted warrior, one who is endowed with exceptional abilities and courage on the battlefield. In Islamic history, Awamir is the name of several prominent companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who demonstrated exceptional valor and leadership.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carrier of blessings and courage in the face of adversity.

in_arabic.name: عوامر
in_arabic.meaning: أمر العامّة، الأمر بالصالح، وسمّى به صديق بني هاشم
in_arabic.long_meaning: عوامر: الأمر العامّة، أو الأمر بالصالح، وهو اسم من أسماء الصالحين، كما يروى أنَّهُ سُمّي به صديق بني هاشم، وهو إسمُ يُشير إلى الأمر بالخير والصالح، والذي هو من أجود الأسماء المقدسة في الإسلام، ويدل على الشخص الذي يؤمَن الناس بالخير والعدل، ويُعتبر اسمًا من الأسماء التي تجذب الإنسان إلى الخير والصالح، وتشير إلى الشخص الذي يمتلك صفات مثل الصدق والعدل والخير، ويُعتبر اسمًا مشهورًا في الإسلام، وممنوحًا من الله تعالى لصديقه بني هاشم، وهو اسمٌ يُشير إلى النفس الصالحة التي تُؤمَن الناس بالخير والعدل، ويُعتبر من الأسماء التي تجذب الإنسان إلى الله تعالى

in_english.name: Awamir
in_english.meaning: General command, order of goodness, and name of Sadik bin Hâshim
in_english.long_meaning: Awamir: The name Awamir refers to a general command or order to do good deeds. It is associated with the name of Sadik bin Hâshim, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. The name Awamir is derived from the Arabic root 'awm', which means 'to order' or 'to command'. In Islamic tradition, the name Awamir is considered a blessed name, as it reflects the qualities of a person who is righteous, just, and kind. The name Awamir is also associated with the concept of 'amr bil-ma'ruf', or the order to do good and forbid evil. A person with the name Awamir is expected to be a leader or a guide who inspires others to do good deeds and follow the right path.

historical_references.reference: The Awamir were a Bedouin tribe who inhabited the central part of the Arabian Peninsula from the 11th to the 16th centuries. They were known for their poetic tradition, which played an important role in preserving the oral history and genealogy of the tribe.

historical_references.reference: The Awamir were also a significant power in the region during the period of the Rasulids, an Islamic dynasty that ruled Yemen from 1225 to 1454. They were allies of the Rasulids and helped them expand their territories by providing military support.
historical_references.context: Significant power in Yemen during Rasulid Islamic dynasty, allies and military supporters
